You are also proficient with one tool of your choice. Whenever you make an ability check with the chosen skill or tool, roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the check's total.

traits.name: Partially Amphibious
traits.description: By absorbing oxygen through your skin, you can breathe underwater for up to 1 hour. Once you've reached that limit, you can't use this trait again until you finish a long rest.

description: Vedalken are tall and slender, standing almost a head taller than humans on average but weighing about the same. Their hairless skin comes in a range of shades of blue, their eyes are darker shades of blue or violet, they lack external ears, their noses are broad and flat, and they are partially amphibious.

Vedalken Dispassion.notes: You have advantage on all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

skill_profs: one skill of your choice: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Performance, or Sleight of Hand
Tireless Precision.notes: Whenever you make an ability check with the chosen skill or tool, roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the check's total.

Partially Amphibious.notes: By absorbing oxygen through your skin, you can breathe underwater for up to 1 hour. Once you've reached that limit, you can't use this trait again until you finish a long rest.

name: Dwarves of the Iron Hills

traits.name: Ability Score Increases
traits.description: Your Constitution and Strength scores increase by 2.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 50 to 100. Dwarves generally start their life on the road in their fifties, and do not usually consider retiring before their nineties. Around that time, they feel they can no longer stay away from their family, or want to dedicate themselves solely to the perfection of their crafts. But Dwarves can remain active until they are more than two hundred years old, and may return to adventuring if a great need arises, like the opportunity to avenge an old insult or injury, or to recover a treasure or reclaim a long-lost dwarf-hold. A healthy Dwarf who avoids a violent death can reach two hundred fifty years of age.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Dwarves generally stand between 4 to 5 feet tall and can weigh upwards of 160 lbs. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 ft. Your speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

traits.name: Night Vision (Dwarf)
traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 ft of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Tools for War
traits.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, mattocks and warhammers.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan’s tools of your choice: jeweller’s tools, mason’s tools, miner’s tools, smith’s tools, or woodcarver’s tools. You also gain proficiency in one musical instrument of your choice.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check, instead of your normal Proficiency Bonus.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

description: The Dwarves of the Iron Hills live the simple but harsh life of miners and smiths. They are often gruff and terse when dealing with outsiders, as choosing to remain on the far eastern edge of the Wild has made them short-spoken, short-tempered and often quick to seek out a physical solution when a threat arises.

Ability Score Increases.notes: Constitution and Strength scores increase by 2.

Adventuring Age.notes: Flavor text about age range (50-100 typical start, up to 250 years).

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

Night Vision (Dwarf).notes: Can see in dim light within 60 ft as if bright light, but cannot see in darkness.

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison.

Tools for War.notes: Proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, mattocks and warhammers. (Mapped to D&D 5e equivalents: Battleaxe, Handaxe, Greataxe, Warhammer, Maul, Light hammer.)

Tool Proficiency.notes: Choose one artisan's tool from the list and one musical instrument.

Stonecunning.notes: Considered proficient in History checks related to stonework origin, and add double proficiency bonus.

Languages.notes: Speak, read, write Dalish and a secret dwarven language.

name: Duergar

traits.name: Duergar Resilience
traits.description: The duergar has advantage on saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions, as well as to resist being charmed or paralyzed.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

description: Duergar are dour, pessimistic, untrusting creatures, always toiling and complaining, with no memory of what it means to be happy or proud. Their craftsmanship and accomplishments endure, yet they are bereft of warmth or artistry.

Duergar Resilience.notes: Has advantage on saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions. The condition immunity only covers Charmed and Paralyzed as explicitly stated; poison and illusions are covered by advantage but not immunity.

Sunlight Sensitivity.notes: While in sunlight, has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

name: Thri-kreen

traits.name: Chameleon Carapace
traits.description: The thri-kreen can change the color of its carapace to match the color and texture of its surroundings. As a result, it has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The thri-kreen's long jump is up to 30 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.description: Armor Class 15 (natural armor)

traits.name: Bite
traits.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also paralyzed while poisoned in this way. The poisoned target can repeat the saving throw on each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Claws
traits.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) slashing damage.

description: Thri-kreen are medium humanoid insectoids with a chitinous carapace, capable of changing color to blend with their surroundings, and possess powerful leaping abilities.

Chameleon Carapace.notes: Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

Standing Leap.notes: Long jump up to 30 feet, high jump up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

Bite.notes: Natural weapon: bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d6+1) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also paralyzed while poisoned. The poisoned target can repeat the saving throw on each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Claws.notes: Natural weapon: claws. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (2d4+1) slashing damage.

name: Alseid

traits.name: Alseid Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with spears and shortbows.

traits.name: Light Hooves
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Stealth skill.

traits.name: Quadruped
traits.description: The mundane details of the structures of humanoids can present considerable obstacles for you. You have to squeeze when moving through trapdoors, manholes, and similar structures even when a Medium humanoid wouldn't have to squeeze. In addition, ladders, stairs, and similar structures are difficult terrain for you.

traits.name: Woodfriend
traits.description: When in a forest, you leave no tracks and can automatically discern true north.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

description: Alseid are tall, antlered humanoids standing over 6 feet tall and weighing around 300 pounds, with a deep connection to the Old World magic of the Margreve forest.

Quadruped.notes: Must squeeze through trapdoors, manholes, and similar structures even when a Medium humanoid wouldn't have to. Ladders, stairs, and similar structures are difficult terrain.

Woodfriend.notes: When in a forest, you leave no tracks and can automatically discern true north.

name: Piney
source: Midgard and Kobold Press, Player's Guide p.10

traits.name: Margreve Within
traits.description: As a piney adventuring beyond the Margreve, you have lost the more extreme, occasionally monstrous, qualities of your forest-dwelling kin. Nonetheless, the magic of the elder forest marks you. You can meet your daily alimentary needs by consuming a suitable amount of food or by standing in direct sunlight for 30 minutes. In addition, your organs are partially made from plant matter. You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Margreve Without
traits.description:
Regardless of the time and distance between you and the Margreve, the forest's influence on you manifests in the form of strange alterations to your body. Although you are humanoid, your connection to the Margreve marks you with plant‑like characteristics. Create a growth of your own in consultation with your GM or pick one from the following list:
•	Your skin is rough with harmless cracks resembling tree bark. 
•	Heavily-perfumed flowers grow wherever your body hair is dense. They can be plucked, but they grow back within a few days.
•	Your eyes are twice as large as a human's, and their color is a changing swirl of green and brown.
•	Your finger and toe nails are wood.
•	Your major joints (shoulder, hip, knee) creak like tree branches when you move.

traits.name: Roots
traits.description: You have a deep and pragmatic connection with the natural world. You are proficient in the Nature and Survival skills.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: A life lived under the canopy of the forest has provided you with the ability to see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

description: Pineys are humanoid beings with plant-like characteristics, such as bark-like skin, wooden nails, or flowers growing from their bodies, and they vary widely in height and build from barely 5 feet to well over 6 feet tall.

Margreve Within.notes: You can meet daily alimentary needs by consuming food or standing in direct sunlight for 30 minutes. You have advantage on saving throws against poison.

Margreve Without.notes: Cosmetic plant-like alterations to your body (choose one: bark-like skin, perfumed flowers, large green-brown eyes, wooden nails, creaking joints).

name: Sea Elf

traits.name: Sea Elf Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the spear, trident, light crossbow, and net.

traits.name: Child of the Sea
traits.description: You have a swimming speed of 30 feet, and you can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Friend of the Sea
traits.description: Using gestures and sounds, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.

description: Sea elves fell in love with the wild beauty of the ocean in the earliest days of the multiverse. Today, they live in small, hidden communities in the ocean shallows and on the Elemental Plane of Water.

Child of the Sea.notes: Swimming speed of 30 feet; can breathe air and water.

Friend of the Sea.notes: Can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed using gestures and sounds.

name: Shadar-kai

traits.name: Necrotic Resistance
traits.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage.

traits.name: Blessing of the Raven Queen
traits.description: As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Starting at 3rd level, you also gain resistance to all damage when you teleport using this trait. The resistance lasts until the start of your next turn. During that time, you appear ghostly and translucent.

description: Sworn to the Raven Queen's service, the mysterious shadar-kai venture into the Material Plane from the Shadowfell to advance her will. Once they were fey like the rest of their elven kin, and now they exist in a strange state between life and death.

Blessing of the Raven Queen.notes: As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Starting at 3rd level, you also gain resistance to all damage when you teleport using this trait. The resistance lasts until the start of your next turn. During that time, you appear ghostly and translucent.

name: Gith

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Intelligence score increases by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Gith reach adulthood in their late teens and live for about a century.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Gith are taller and leaner than humans, with most a slender 6 feet in height.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Gith.

traits.name: Subrace
traits.description: There are two kinds of gith, githyanki and githzerai. Choose one of these subraces.

subraces.name: Githyanki

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Strength score increases by 2.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Githyanki tend toward lawful evil. They are aggressive and arrogant, and they remain the faithful servants of their lich-queen, Vlaakith. Renegade githyanki tend toward chaos.

traits.name: Decadent Mastery
traits.description: You learn one language of your choice, and you are proficient with one skill or tool of your choice. In the timeless city of Tu'narath, githyanki have bountiful time to master odd bits of knowledge.

traits.name: Martial Prodigy
traits.description: You are proficient with light and medium armor and with shortswords, longswords, and greatswords.

traits.name: Githyanki Psionics
traits.description: You know the mage hand cantrip, and the hand is invisible when you cast the cantrip with this trait. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the jump spell once with this trait, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. When you reach 5th level, you can cast the misty step spell once with this trait, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells. When you cast them with this trait, they don't require components.

subraces.description: The brutal githyanki are trained from birth as warriors.

subraces.name: Githzerai

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 2.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Githzerai tend toward lawful neutral. Their rigorous training in psychic abilities requires an implacable mental discipline.

traits.name: Mental Discipline
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against the charmed and frightened conditions. Under the tutelage of monastic masters, githzerai learn to govern their own minds.

traits.name: Githzerai Psionics
traits.description: You know the mage hand cantrip, and the hand is invisible when you cast the cantrip with this trait. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the shield spell once with this trait, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. When you reach 5th level, you can cast the detect thoughts spell once with this trait, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells. When you cast them with this trait, they don't require components.

subraces.description: In their fortresses within Limbo, the githzerai hone their minds to a razor's edge.

description: Gith are taller and leaner than humans, with most a slender 6 feet in height.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Intelligence score increases by 1.

Age.notes: Gith reach adulthood in their late teens and live for about a century.

Size.notes: Gith are taller and leaner than humans, with most a slender 6 feet in height.

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Common and Gith.

Subrace.notes: Choose between githyanki and githzerai subrace.

name: Wood Elf

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Elf Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.

traits.name: Fleet of Foot
traits.description: Your base walking speed increases to 35 feet.

traits.name: Mask of the Wild
traits.description: You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

description: Wood elves are a reclusive and graceful race, known for their keen senses and affinity for nature.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Wisdom score increases by 1.

Mask of the Wild.notes: Can attempt to hide when only lightly obscured by natural phenomena (foliage, rain, snow, mist, etc.).

name: Dark Elf (Drow)

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Charisma score increases by 1.

traits.name: Superior Darkvision
traits.description: Your darkvision has a radius of 120 feet.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

traits.name: Drow Magic
traits.description: You know the dancing lights cantrip. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the faerie fire spell once per day. When you reach 5th level, you can also cast the darkness spell once per day. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Drow Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with rapiers, shortswords, and hand crossbows.

description: Dark elves, also called drow, have black skin that resembles polished obsidian and stark white or pale yellow hair, with very pale eyes in shades of lilac, silver, pink, red, and blue. They tend to be smaller and thinner than most elves.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Charisma score increases by 1.

Sunlight Sensitivity.notes: Disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when in direct sunlight.

Drow Magic.notes: Knows dancing lights cantrip. At 3rd level, can cast faerie fire once per day. At 5th level, can cast darkness once per day. Charisma is spellcasting ability.

name: Woodmen of Mountain Hall

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Strength score increases by 1, and you may increase two additional ability scores by 1.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 16-30. Those of Firienseld don't usually venture far from the Burg until their 16th year and rarely continue past their fortieth year, when the desire to return to the mountains of their youth becomes strong.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Most Woodmen are between 5 and 6 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Mountainfolk
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Survival skill.

traits.name: Virtue
traits.description: You gain one Woodmen of Mountain Hall Cultural Virtue (see below) of your choice.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You speak the Vale of Anduin tongue, an archaic version of Westron, closely related to Dalish.

description: The folk of Firienseld are close kin with those who live under the eaves of Mirkwood and share both their physical appearance and naming conventions.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Strength score increases by 1, and you may increase two additional ability scores by 1.

Virtue.notes: Gain one Woodmen of Mountain Hall Cultural Virtue of your choice.

Languages.notes: Speaks Vale of Anduin tongue (archaic Westron, related to Dalish).

name: Wild Hobbit

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2 and you may increase any two other ability scores by 1.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 25-60. Wild Hobbits value family above all else and have a deep and abiding distrust of outsiders. Those who venture out are either young and taking desperate chances or have had some calamity foisted upon them. Around their fiftieth year, even the most ambitious Wild Hobbits think seriously of finding a hidden refuge and attending to their family's needs.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Like their civilised kin, Wild Hobbits are Small.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

traits.name: Untroubled by Shadows
traits.description: When in a blighted area, you must make a DC 5 Wisdom saving throw to avoid Shadow instead of the regular DC 15.

traits.name: Hobbit Nimbleness
traits.description: You can move through the space of any creature who is at least one size larger than yours.

traits.name: Clever Beyond Compare
traits.description: You have proficiency in either the Investigation or the Riddle skill.

traits.name: Hobbit Elusiveness
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Stealth skill.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You speak the Vale of Anduin tongue, an archaic version of Westron that is also spoken by Beornings and Woodmen.

description: Wild Hobbits are small, lean folk with sharp, untrusting eyes, rarely plump except for elders, and they always carry simple tools of survival such as fishing tackle and hand tools, moving about the watercourses of the Vales of Anduin on little boats of reeds.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Dexterity increases by 2; two other ability scores increase by 1.

Untroubled by Shadows.notes: In blighted areas, DC 5 Wisdom save to avoid Shadow instead of DC 15.

Hobbit Nimbleness.notes: Can move through space of creatures at least one size larger.

Clever Beyond Compare.notes: Choose one of the two skills.

Languages.notes: Speaks Vale of Anduin tongue.

name: High Elf of Rivendell

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 2 and you may increase any two other attributes by 1 each.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 500 to 1000. The High Elves of Rivendell are creatures from another age. They may become adventurers any time after they reach adulthood, although they are unlikely to venture beyond Imladris until they are half a millennia or more old. Even though a starting High Elf is far more 'experienced' than those of other cultures, he is still young and weak compared to his elder kin, and so is unlikely to be more than a thousand years old.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Elves range from 5 to over 6 feet tall, with slender builds. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Night Vision
traits.description: Accustomed to walking under the revered starlight, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.

traits.name: The Eyes of Elves
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

traits.name: Elvish Dreams
traits.description: Your sleep is not like that of mortals. When you sleep, you can choose to send your mind into an "Elvish Dream" retaining full consciousness of your surroundings and you needn't close your eyes. Four hours spent in such dreams acts on you as if you had rested an entire night.

traits.name: Against the Unseen
traits.description: High Elves can perceive creatures that dwell in the wraith-world, be they spirits or ghosts, even when they are normally Invisible to the eyes of the living (including Unclad and Invisible Ringwraiths). Additionally, High Elves are immune to the Frightened condition when the source of that condition is an undead creature.

traits.name: Elf-wise
traits.description: You have fought against the Dark Lord for years uncounted, and will continue to strive against the Enemy. You are proficient in Corruption checks. A Corruption check is any Wisdom saving throw that risks 1 or more Shadow points for failure.

traits.name: Beset by Woe
traits.description: High Elves cannot ever truly forget the taint of the Shadow once it has left its mark on their spirit. Whenever you undertake to Heal Corruption, you

description: The High Elves of Rivendell are a noble and ancient people, known for their grace, wisdom, and deep connection to the lore of Middle-earth.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Wisdom score increases by 2; may increase any two other attributes by 1 each.

Adventuring Age.notes: Flavor text about age range (500-1000 years) for starting High Elves.

Elvish Dreams.notes: Requires only 4 hours of trance (Elvish Dream) to gain benefits of a long rest; remains conscious of surroundings during trance.

Against the Unseen.notes: Can perceive invisible undead/spirits (e.g., Ringwraiths). Immunity to Frightened condition only when the source is an undead creature.

Elf-wise.notes: Proficient in Corruption checks (Wisdom saving throws that risk Shadow points).

Beset by Woe.notes: Flavor text about healing Corruption; incomplete description.

name: High Elves of Rivendell

traits.name: Beset by Woe
traits.description: High Elves cannot ever truly forget the taint of the Shadow once it has left its mark on their spirit. Whenever you undertake to Heal Corruption, you immediately lose 1 point of temporary Shadow and gain 1 point of permanent Shadow. You may then make an ability check to remove temporary Shadow points as normal (see page 200 of the Player’s Guide).

traits.name: The Tools of War
traits.description: You have proficiency with daggers, spears, great spears, short swords, long swords, short bows and great bows.

traits.name: Subtlety of Craft
traits.description: You have proficiency in one artisan’s tool of your choice.

traits.name: Corruption Check Proficiency
traits.description: You are proficient in Corruption checks. A Corruption check is any Wisdom saving throw that risks 1 or more Shadow points for failure.

description: The High Elves of Rivendell are a noble and ancient people, known for their grace, wisdom, and deep connection to the lore of Middle-earth.

Beset by Woe.notes: When you undertake to Heal Corruption, you immediately lose 1 point of temporary Shadow and gain 1 point of permanent Shadow. You may then make an ability check to remove temporary Shadow points as normal.

tool_profs: One artisan's tool of your choice

Corruption Check Proficiency.notes: You are proficient in Corruption checks (Wisdom saving throws that risk 1 or more Shadow points for failure).

name: Gold Dwarf

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

traits.name: Dwarven Combat Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan's tools of your choice: smith's tools, brewer's supplies, or mason's tools.

subraces.name: Hill Dwarf

traits.name: Dwarven Toughness
traits.description: Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.

subraces.description: Gold dwarves have the racial traits of hill dwarves in the Player's Handbook.

description: Gold dwarves are stocky and muscular, averaging about 4 feet tall, with brown skin, black or brown hair, and brown or hazel eyes, with green eyes rare (and considered lucky). Males grow full beards that they keep oiled and well groomed, and both genders wear their hair long and often elaborately braided.

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison.

Stonecunning.notes: Considered proficient in History checks related to stonework origin, and adds double proficiency bonus to such checks.

Tool Proficiency.notes: Choose one of the listed artisan's tools.

name: Gray Dwarf (Duergar)

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

traits.name: Dwarven Combat Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan's tools of your choice: smith's tools, brewer's supplies, or mason's tools.

subraces.name: Duergar

traits.name: Superior Darkvision
traits.description: Your darkvision has a radius of 120 feet.

traits.name: Extra Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Undercommon.

traits.name: Duergar Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against illusions and against being charmed or paralyzed.

traits.name: Duergar Magic
traits.description: When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the enlarge/reduce spell on yourself once with this trait, using only the spell's enlarge option. When you reach 5th level, you can cast the invisibility spell on yourself once with this trait. You don't need material components for either spell, and you can't cast them while you're in direct sunlight, although sunlight has no effect on them once cast. You regain the ability to cast these spells with this trait when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

subraces.description: The gray dwarves, or duergar, live deep in the Underdark. They are wiry and lean, with black eyes and bald heads, with the males growing long, unkempt, gray beards.

description: Gray dwarves (duergar) are grim, ashen-skinned dwarves who live in the Underdark, valuing toil above all else and disdaining aesthetic or artistic value.

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.

Stonecunning.notes: When making an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient and add double your proficiency bonus.

Tool Proficiency.notes: You gain proficiency with one of the listed artisan's tools of your choice.

name: Strongheart Halfling

traits.name: Lucky
traits.description: When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

traits.name: Brave
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

traits.name: Halfling Nimbleness
traits.description: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

traits.name: Stout Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

description: Strongheart halflings are shorter on average than their lightfoot kin, and tend to have rounder faces. They have the skin tones and hair colors of humans, with most having brown hair.

Lucky.notes: When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

Halfling Nimbleness.notes: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

Stout Resilience.notes: You have advantage on saving throws against poison.

name: Ghostwise Halflings

traits.name: Silent Speech
traits.description: You can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of you. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time.

description: Ghostwise halflings are a reclusive and silent subrace of halflings, known for their telepathic communication and deep connection to nature.

Silent Speech.notes: You can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of you. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time.

name: Tortle

traits.name: Claws
traits.description: Your claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: You can hold your breath for up to 1 hour at a time. Tortles aren't natural swimmers, but they can remain underwater for some time before needing to come up for air.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.description: Due to your shell and the shape of your body, you are ill-suited to wearing armor. Your shell provides ample protection, however; it gives you a base AC of 17 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You gain no benefit from wearing armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield's bonus as normal.

traits.name: Shell Defense
traits.description: You can withdraw into your shell as an action. Until you emerge, you gain a +4 bonus to AC and you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws. While in your shell, you are prone, your speed is 0 and can't increase, you have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws, you can't take reactions, and the only action you can take is a bonus action to emerge from your shell.

traits.name: Survival Instinct
traits.description: You gain proficiency in the Survival skill. Tortles have finely honed survival instincts.

description: Tortles are humanoid tortoises that stand 5 to 6 feet tall and average 450 pounds. They have a shell that provides natural armor and are known for their longevity and survival instincts.

Claws.notes: Your claws are natural weapons. You can make unarmed strikes with them, dealing 1d4 + Strength modifier slashing damage instead of normal bludgeoning damage.

Hold Breath.notes: You can hold your breath for up to 1 hour at a time.

Natural Armor.notes: You gain no benefit from wearing armor, but can use a shield normally.

Shell Defense.notes: As an action, withdraw into shell: +4 AC, advantage on Strength and Constitution saves, prone, speed 0, disadvantage on Dexterity saves, no reactions, only action is bonus action to emerge.

name: Firbolg

traits.name: Firbolg Magic
traits.description: You can cast detect magic and disguise self with this trait, using Wisdom as your spellcasting ability for them. Once you cast either spell, you can't cast it again with this trait until you finish a short or long rest. When you use this version of disguise self, you can seem up to 3 feet shorter than normal, allowing you to more easily blend in with humans and elves.

traits.name: Hidden Step
traits.description: As a bonus action, you can magically turn invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack, make a damage roll, or force someone to make a saving throw. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.description: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Speech of Beast and Leaf
traits.description: You have the ability to communicate in a limited manner with beasts and plants. They can understand the meaning of your words, though you have no special ability to understand them in return. You have advantage on all Charisma checks you make to influence them.

description: Firbolg are between 7 and 8 feet tall and weigh between 240 and 300 pounds. They are humanoids related to the fey, with long lifespans, and typically follow the rhythm of nature as its caretakers.

Firbolg Magic.notes: Can cast detect magic and disguise self (Wisdom-based). Once per short or long rest each. Disguise self can make you appear up to 3 feet shorter.

Hidden Step.notes: As a bonus action, become invisible until start of next turn or until you attack, deal damage, or force a saving throw. Once per short or long rest.

Powerful Build.notes: Count as one size larger for carrying capacity and push/drag/lift weight.

Speech of Beast and Leaf.notes: Can communicate limitedly with beasts and plants; they understand your words but you cannot understand them. Advantage on Charisma checks to influence them.

name: Kenku

traits.name: Expert Forgery
traits.description: You can duplicate other creatures' handwriting and craftwork. You have advantage on all checks made to produce forgeries or duplicates of existing objects.

traits.name: Kenku Training
traits.description: You are proficient in your choice of two of the following skills: Acrobatics, Deception, Stealth, and Sleight of Hand.

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.description: You can mimic sounds you have heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds you make can tell they are imitations with a successful Wisdom (Insight) check opposed by your Charisma (Deception) check.

description: Kenku are around 5 feet tall and weigh between 90 and 120 pounds. They are chaotic creatures, rarely making enduring commitments, and care mostly for preserving their own hides.

Expert Forgery.notes: Advantage on all checks to produce forgeries or duplicates of existing objects.

Kenku Training.notes: Choose two of the listed skills to gain proficiency in.

Mimicry.notes: Can mimic sounds and voices; opposed check to detect imitation.

name: Lizardfolk

traits.name: Bite
traits.description: Your fanged maw is a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Cunning Artisan
traits.description: As part of a short rest, you can harvest bone and hide from a slain beast, construct, dragon, monstrosity, or plant creature of size Small or larger to create one of the following items: a shield, a club, a javelin, or 1d4 darts or blowgun needles. To use this trait, you need a blade, such as a dagger, or appropriate artisan's tools, such as leatherworker's tools.

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes at a time.

traits.name: Hunter's Lore
traits.description: You gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.description: You have tough, scaly skin. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

traits.name: Hungry Jaws
traits.description: In battle, you can throw yourself into a vicious feeding frenzy. As a bonus action, you can make a special attack with your bite. If the attack hits, it deals its normal damage, and you gain temporary hit points (minimum of 1) equal to your Constitution modifier, and you can't use this trait again until you finish a short or long rest.

description: Lizardfolk are a little bulkier and taller than humans, and their colorful frills make them appear even larger.

Bite.notes: Natural weapon: fanged maw (unarmed strike, 1d6 piercing damage + Strength modifier instead of normal bludgeoning).

Cunning Artisan.notes: During a short rest, can harvest bone/hide from a slain creature (size Small or larger, type beast/construct/dragon/monstrosity/plant) to create a shield, club, javelin, or 1d4 darts/blowgun needles. Requires a blade or appropriate artisan's tools.

Hold Breath.notes: Can hold breath for up to 15 minutes.

Hunter's Lore.notes: Choose two of the listed skills to gain proficiency in.

Natural Armor.notes: Natural armor (scaly skin). AC = 13 + Dexterity modifier when not wearing armor. Shield benefits apply normally.

Hungry Jaws.notes: Bonus action: special bite attack. If hits, deals normal bite damage and gain temporary HP equal to Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Cannot use again until after a short or long rest.

name: Tabaxi

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You have a cat's keen senses, especially in the dark. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Feline Agility
traits.description: Your reflexes and agility allow you to move with a burst of speed. When you move on your turn in combat, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns.

traits.name: Cat's Claws
traits.description: Because of your claws, you have a climbing speed of 20 feet. In addition, your claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Cat's Talent
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Perception and Stealth skills.

description: Tabaxi are taller on average than humans and relatively slender. They have cat-like features and a natural curiosity.

Feline Agility.notes: Once per turn, can double speed until end of turn. Recharges when you move 0 feet on a turn.

Cat's Claws.notes: Climbing speed of 20 feet. Natural weapons (claws): unarmed strike deals 1d4 + Strength slashing damage.

name: Triton

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Strength, Constitution, and Charisma scores each increase by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Tritons reach maturity around age 15 and can live up to 200 years.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Tritons tend toward lawful good. As guardians of the darkest reaches of the sea, their culture pushes them toward order and benevolence.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Tritons are slightly shorter than humans, averaging about 5 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a swimming speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: You can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Control Air and Water
traits.description: A child of the sea, you can call on the magic of elemental air and water. You can cast fog cloud with this trait. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast gust of wind with it, and starting at 5th level, you can also cast wall of water with it (see the spell in the sidebar). Once you cast a spell with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Emissary of the Sea
traits.description: Aquatic beasts have an extraordinary affinity with your people. You can communicate simple ideas with beasts that can breathe water. They can understand the meaning of your words, though you have no special ability to understand them in return.

traits.name: Guardians of the Depths
traits.description: Adapted to even the most extreme ocean depths, you have resistance to cold damage, and you ignore any of the drawbacks caused by a deep, underwater environment.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Primordial.

description: Tritons are slightly shorter than humans, averaging about 5 feet tall, and are guardians of the darkest reaches of the sea.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Strength, Constitution, and Charisma scores each increase by 1.

Age.notes: Tritons reach maturity around age 15 and can live up to 200 years.

Control Air and Water.notes: Can cast fog cloud (at will), gust of wind (3rd level), and wall of water (5th level) once per long rest. Charisma is spellcasting ability.

Emissary of the Sea.notes: Can communicate simple ideas with beasts that can breathe water.

Guardians of the Depths.notes: Ignores drawbacks caused by deep, underwater environments.

Languages.notes: Speaks, reads, and writes Common and Primordial.

name: Bugbear

traits.name: Long-Limbed
traits.description: When you make a melee attack on your turn, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.description: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Sneaky
traits.description: You are proficient in the Stealth skill.

traits.name: Surprise Attack
traits.description: If you surprise a creature and hit it with an attack on your first turn in combat, the attack deals an extra 2d6 damage to it. You can use this trait only once per combat.

description: Bugbears are between 6 and 8 feet tall and weigh between 250 and 350 pounds. They endure a harsh existence that demands each of them to remain self-sufficient, even at the expense of their fellows.

Long-Limbed.notes: Your reach for melee attacks is 5 feet greater than normal.

Powerful Build.notes: You count as one size larger when determining carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

Surprise Attack.notes: If you surprise a creature and hit it with an attack on your first turn in combat, the attack deals an extra 2d6 damage. Can be used only once per combat.

name: Hobgoblin

traits.name: Martial Training
traits.description: You are proficient with two martial weapons of your choice and with light armor.

traits.name: Saving Face
traits.description: Hobgoblins are careful not to show weakness in front of their allies, for fear of losing status. If you miss with an attack roll or fail an ability check or a saving throw, you can gain a bonus to the roll equal to the number of allies you can see within 30 feet of you (maximum bonus of +5). Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

description: Hobgoblins are between 5 and 6 feet tall and weigh between 150 and 200 pounds. They are Medium-sized humanoids with a rigid, militaristic society.

weapon_profs: Two martial weapons of your choice

Saving Face.notes: If you miss with an attack roll or fail an ability check or a saving throw, you can gain a bonus to the roll equal to the number of allies you can see within 30 feet of you (maximum bonus of +5). Once used, cannot be used again until finishing a short or long rest.

name: Kobold

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Grovel, Cower, and Bes
traits.description: As an action on your tum, you can cower pathetically to distract nearby foes. Until the end of your next turn, your allies gain advantage on attack rolls against enemies within 10 feet of you that can see you. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: You have advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

description: Kobolds are between 2 and 3 feet tall and weigh between 25 and 35 pounds. They are small, reptilian humanoids with a selfish and lawful evil alignment.

name: Orc

traits.name: Aggressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, you can move up to your speed toward an enemy of your choice that you can see or hear. You must end this move closer to the enemy than you started.

traits.name: Menacing
traits.description: You are trained in the Intimidation skill.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.description: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

description: No description available.

name: Yuan-ti Pureblood

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description: You know the poison spray cantrip. You can cast animal friendship an unlimited number of times with this trait, but you can target only snakes with it. Starting at 3rd level, you can also cast suggestion with this trait. Once you cast it, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Poison Immunity
traits.description: You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

description: Purebloods match humans in average size and weight. They are devoid of emotion and see others as tools to manipulate.

Innate Spellcasting.notes: Knows poison spray cantrip. Can cast animal friendship unlimited times (snakes only). At 3rd level, can cast suggestion once per long rest. Charisma is spellcasting ability.

Magic Resistance.notes: Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

name: Grung

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The grung can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Poisonous Skin
traits.description: Any creature that grapples the grung or otherwise comes into direct contact with the grung's skin must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature no longer in direct contact with the grung can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The grung's long jump is up to 25 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

traits.name: Water Dependency
traits.description: A grung that fails to immerse itself in water for at least 1 hour during a day suffers one level of exhaustion at the end of that day. A grung can recover from this exhaustion only through magic or by immersing itself in water for at least 1 hour.

description: Grungs are small, poisonous frog-like humanoids that live in hierarchical caste societies and are known for their toxic skin and ability to leap great distances.

Poisonous Skin.notes: Any creature that grapples the grung or otherwise comes into direct contact with the grung's skin must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature no longer in direct contact with the grung can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Standing Leap.notes: Long jump up to 25 feet, high jump up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

Water Dependency.notes: Must immerse in water for at least 1 hour per day or suffer one level of exhaustion at the end of that day. Exhaustion can only be recovered via magic or by immersing in water for at least 1 hour.

name: Tlincalli
description: Tlincallis, also called scorpion folk, are chitin-covered creatures, humanoid from the waist up with the lower body of an enormous scorpion, complete with a stinger at the end of a long tail.

name: Xvart

traits.name: Low Cunning
traits.description: The xvart can take the Disengage action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

traits.name: Overbearing Pack
traits.description: The xvart has advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to shove a creature if at least one of the xvart's allies is within 5 feet of the target and the ally isn't incapacitated.

traits.name: Raxivort's Tongue
traits.description: The xvart can communicate with ordinary bats and rats, as well as giant bats and giant rats.

description: Xvarts are small, chaotic evil humanoids with a greedy and cowardly nature, often found in the company of giant rats and bats.

Low Cunning.notes: Can take the Disengage action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

Overbearing Pack.notes: Has advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to shove a creature if at least one ally is within 5 feet of the target and the ally isn't incapacitated.

Raxivort's Tongue.notes: Can communicate with ordinary bats and rats, as well as giant bats and giant rats.

name: Riverfolk Halfling
source: Riverfolk: The Scattered People of the Trade p.12-14

traits.name: Lucky
traits.description: When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

traits.name: Brave
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

traits.name: Halfling Nimbleness
traits.description: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

traits.name: Preternatural Navigator
traits.description: You have an inherent connection to ley lines. You can sense the presence of a ley line within 1 mile of you. Additionally, you can cast the misty step spell once per long rest, but only to teleport to a location you can see that is on or adjacent to a ley line.

traits.name: Animal Ken
traits.description: You have advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks. Additionally, you can communicate simple concepts to beasts, and they can communicate simple concepts back to you.

traits.name: Riverfolk Toughness
traits.description: You have proficiency with water vehicles and with the following tools: navigator's tools.

description: Riverfolk are city halflings, usually growing up on docks, fishing boats, and the patchwork barges. Most are more at home on a temperamental river than on solid ground, and riverfolk seldom fear drowning.

Riverfolk Toughness.notes: You have proficiency with water vehicles.

name: Courtfolk

traits.name: Boon Companion
traits.description: You are quick to step in and help your friends, and you have a knack for knowing exactly how to best do it. When you work with an ally to complete a task or take the Help action in combat, your ally adds a d4 to their check or attack roll (this includes the second roll made with advantage).

traits.name: Wee Glamour
traits.description: You are—ever so slightly—imbued with a bit of elven magic. You move with grace, your laugh is always pleasant, and colors are more vibrant on you. Your Charisma score increases by 1, and you have advantage on saves against spells of the enchantment school.

description: Courtfolk are halflings with obvious elven influence, mired in elven culture for generations, with shorter, softer names than elves and a lilting flair.

Boon Companion.notes: When you take the Help action or work with an ally on a task, the ally adds a d4 to their check or attack roll (including the second roll made with advantage).

Wee Glamour.notes: Charisma score increases by 1. Advantage on saving throws against spells of the enchantment school.

subraces.name: Shadow Servitors

traits.name: Disquiet
traits.description: You still look like your old self, but your mind is changed by the knowledge you’ve accepted—and you’re not sure it’s for the better. Your Intelligence score increases by 1. Additionally, something in your eyes makes people uneasy around you. You have advantage on Charisma (Intimidate) and Charisma (Deception) checks against humanoids.

traits.name: Silent Steps
traits.description: You’ve always been adept at evading notice, but now your own shadow seems to muffle the noise you make. You can cast the silence spell once per day centered on yourself, which you can end at any time by speaking. Additionally, you always have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to be quiet.

subraces.description: Those courtfolk who elect to serve shadow fey are usually broken spirits to start with, and over time, the cracks in their souls become filled with something darker.

description: Courtfolk are the longest-lived of the halfling subraces, perhaps owing to their close association with elves. They are at home in elven courts and politics and have had generations to practice the art of remaining unnoticed until needed.

name: Windrunner Elf
description: Elusive, eccentric, and unpredictable, windrunner elves have quietly traversed Midgard’s vast central grasslands for millennia. These diminutive nomads roaming the steppes and plains are thought to originally hail from the elven capital of Sephaya.

name: Changeling
source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War p.59

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Charisma score increases by 2, and either your Dexterity or your Intelligence increases by 1 (your choice).

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Changelings mature slightly faster than humans but share a similar lifespan—typically a century or less. While a changeling can shapeshift to appear younger, they age at the same rate as humans, and the effects of aging are up to them.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Changelings hate to be bound in any way, and those who follow the path of the Traveler believe that chaos and change are important aspects of life. Most tend toward pragmatic neutrality as opposed to being concerned with lofty ideals. Despite common fears, few changelings embrace evil.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: In their natural forms, changelings average between 5 to 6 feet in height, with a slender build. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Age.notes: Flavor/roleplay trait only; no mechanical effect.

name: Kalashtar
source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War p.59

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom and Charisma scores both increase by 1. In addition, one ability score of your choice increases by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Kalashtar develop physically at the same rate as humans do and have similar lifespans.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: The noble spirit tied to a kalashtar drives it toward lawful and good behavior. Most kalashtar combine strong self-discipline with compassion for all sentient beings, but some kalashtar resist the virtuous influence of their spirit.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Kalashtar are similar in build to humans, though they are typically a few inches taller. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Dual Mind
traits.description: When you make a Wisdom saving throw, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on the roll. You can use this trait immediately before or after you roll, but before any of the roll's effects occur.

traits.name: Mental Discipline
traits.description: You have resistance to psychic damage.

traits.name: Mind Link
traits.description: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You don’t need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic messages, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself. As a bonus action when you’re speaking telepathically to a creature, you can give that creature the ability to speak telepathically to you until the start of your next turn. To use this ability, the creature must be within 60 feet of you and be able to see you.

traits.name: Psychic Glamour
traits.description: Choose one of the following skills: Insight, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have advantage on all ability checks you make with that skill.

traits.name: Severed from Dreams
traits.description: Kalashtar sleep, but they don’t connect to the plane of dreams as other creatures do. Instead, their minds draw from the memories of their otherworldly spirit while they sleep. As such, you are immune to magical spells and effects that require you to dream, like the dream spell, but not to spells and effects that put you to sleep, like the sleep spell.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common, Quori, and one other language of your choice.

description: Kalashtar are similar in build to humans, though they are typically a few inches taller. They have a dual nature, tied to a spirit from the plane of dreams.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Wisdom and Charisma scores both increase by 1. In addition, one ability score of your choice increases by 1.

Age.notes: Kalashtar develop physically at the same rate as humans and have similar lifespans.

Dual Mind.notes: When you make a Wisdom saving throw, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on the roll. You can use this trait immediately before or after you roll, but before you know the outcome.

Mind Link.notes: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet. As a bonus action, you can allow a creature within 60 feet to speak telepathically back to you until the start of your next turn.

Psychic Glamour.notes: Choose one of Insight, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have advantage on all ability checks with that skill.

Severed from Dreams.notes: Immune to the sleep spell and effects that put you to sleep via dream manipulation.

Languages.notes: You can speak, read, and write Common, Quori, and one other language of your choice.

name: Shifter
source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War p.59

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Shifters are quick to mature both physically and emotionally, reaching young adulthood at age 10. They rarely live to be more than 70 years old.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Shifters tend toward neutrality, being more focused on survival than concepts of good and evil. A love of personal freedom can drive shifters toward chaotic alignments.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Shifters range from 5 to almost 7 feet tall, depending on their subrace. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

traits.name: Shifting
traits.description: As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point). You also gain a benefit based on your shifter subrace, described below. Once you shift, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common.

traits.name: Subrace
traits.description: The beast within shapes each shifter physically and mentally. Four major subraces of shifter are found among the worlds of D&D: Beasthide, Longtooth, Swiftstride, and Wildhunt. Choose one of these subraces.

description: Shifters are humanoids with a bestial aspect, ranging from 5 to almost 7 feet tall, who can temporarily assume a more bestial appearance.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Dexterity score increases by 1.

Age.notes: Flavor text only: reach young adulthood at 10, rarely live past 70.

Alignment.notes: Flavor text only: tend toward neutrality, chaotic leanings.

Darkvision.notes: Cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Shifting.notes: As a bonus action, gain temporary HP equal to level + Con mod (min 1) for 1 minute. Additional benefits depend on subrace. Can be used once per short/long rest.

Languages.notes: Speak, read, and write Common.

Subrace.notes: Choose one of: Beasthide, Longtooth, Swiftstride, Wildhunt. Each provides additional traits not detailed here.

name: Warforged
source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War p.59

traits.name: Warforged Resilience
traits.description:
You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:
• You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage.
• You are immune to disease.
• You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
• You don't need to sleep and magic can't put you to sleep.

traits.name: Sentry's Rest
traits.description: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn't render you unconscious, and you can see and hear as normal.

traits.name: Integrated Protection
traits.description: Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You gain no benefit from wearing armor, but if you are using a shield, you apply its bonus as normal. You can alter your body to enter different defensive modes; each time you finish a long rest, choose one mode to adopt from the Integrated Protection table, provided you meet the mode's prerequisite.

description: Warforged are sentient constructs built for military service, standing between 5 and 6 1/2 feet tall, with a body of composite materials and a living, sentient mind.

Warforged Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. Immune to disease. Doesn't need to eat, drink, or breathe. Doesn't need to sleep and magic can't put you to sleep.

Sentry's Rest.notes: During a long rest, you spend at least 6 hours in an inactive, motionless state (not sleeping); you remain conscious and can see and hear normally.

Integrated Protection.notes: Your body has built-in defensive layers that determine your AC. You gain no benefit from wearing armor, but you can use a shield normally. Each time you finish a long rest, choose a defensive mode from the Integrated Protection table (prerequisites apply).
